title: The six asset classes and their risk
desc: What you can trade, from lower to higher risk

cards.title: Where does a bad day cost less?
cards.situation: You’re new and have $1,000 to practice with. You will make mistakes. Where does one bad day cost you less?

items.label: A · Broad index ETF
items.sub: Moves about 1% on a normal day

options.feedback: Smaller swings make each beginner mistake cheaper, so you can afford to learn.
Big swings cut both ways, and beginners make more mistakes.
A 1% day and a 10% day are very different on the same $1,000. Bigger swings mean bigger bad days.

cards.title: What do you actually own?
cards.text: Tap each tile to see what you own in each [[asset-class|asset class]].

items.title: Bonds
items.text: A loan to a government or company. Pays interest.

items.title: Broad index ETFs
items.text: A basket of many companies in one ticker. An ETF is only as calm as what it holds.

items.title: Forex
items.text: One currency against another, like EUR/USD.

items.title: Crypto
items.text: Digital tokens like BTC and ETH. Trades 24/7.

cards.title: Lower risk to higher risk
cards.text: **[[volatility|Volatility]]** is how much a price swings. Higher possible reward usually comes with **higher risk**.

blocks.tip: Forex prices usually move slowly, but most people trade it with borrowed money (leverage). That makes it risky. More in Chapter 2.

cards.title: The fast lane?
cards.myth: Crypto and forex with leverage are the fastest way to get rich.
cards.reality: They’re the riskiest. Big swings, or borrowed money, make mistakes as big as wins, and beginners make more mistakes. Most professionals learn on lower-risk, liquid assets first.

cards.title: Sort by risk
cards.q: Drag each asset class into the right box.

itemFeedback.Forex: Forex prices move slowly, so on its own it sits in the middle. Leverage is what makes it risky.
itemFeedback.Crypto: Crypto swings the most: young, very volatile, and it never sleeps.
itemFeedback.Stocks: One company can move a lot more than a bond or a basket, but less than crypto: the middle.
itemFeedback.Commodities: Oil and gold swing more than bonds, less than crypto: the middle.
itemFeedback.Broad index ETFs: A broad index ETF holds hundreds of companies, so one bad company hurts less. That’s why it sits with bonds. A leveraged or crypto ETF would not.

cards.right: Bonds and broad index ETFs are lower risk, stocks, commodities and forex sit in the middle, and crypto is the riskiest.

cards.title: Which is the riskiest?
cards.q: Your friend wants to practice with his first $500. Which of these usually carries the most risk?

options.feedback: A government bond is a loan that pays interest. It’s one of the calmest choices, not the riskiest.
An index ETF spreads your money over many companies, so it swings less than any one of them.
Large company shares do move. A brand-new coin can swing far more, and few people trade it, so getting out can be hard.
A brand-new coin can swing far more than the others, and few people trade it, so getting out can be hard.

cards.headline: You can rank what you trade by risk.
lines: From calmer to wilder: bonds and broad index ETFs, then stocks, commodities and forex, then crypto.
More possible reward usually means more risk.
Practice on lower-risk, liquid assets first.
